home.name: John Gibson
home.news: Gibson had a tremendous inaugural season with the Red Wings in 2025-26, nearly leading them to a postseason berth, but 2026-27 has started rocky for the team, including Gibson. The 33-year-old American goalie struggled in his previous outing, allowing four goals on 25 shots (.840 SV%) in a 4-1 loss to the Calgary Flames. Gibson has an ugly 3.44 GAA and .867 SV% in eight games this season (3-4-1). The Red Wings enter Thursday's outing as -161 home favourites against a Chicago Blackhawks team that has scored two or fewer goals in four straight games (1-3-0).

away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Impressive early-season performances from Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson made Connor Hellebuyck's suspension (and eventual trade) an afterthought, but recent struggles have become overpowering. Skinner has lost three straight (0-2-1), but has remained serviceable, posting a 2.30 GAA and .920 SV%. He has a 2.60 GAA and .911 SV% in eight games (3-2-3). The Jets enter Thursday's game as significant +203 road underdogs against a Tampa Bay Lightning team on a two-game losing streak (0-1-1).

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Vasilevskiy boasts a 5-3-0 record through eight games, but hasn't lived up to the standard he set last season when he won his second Vezina Trophy. The 32-year-old Russian goalie allowed five goals on 23 shots (.783 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 6-3 loss to the Colorado Avalanche. He has uncharacteristically allowed three or more goals in five of eight games this season, posting a pedestrian 2.78 GAA and .884 SV%. Still, Tampa Bay enters Thursday's game as sizeable -228 home favourites against a struggling Winnipeg Jets team that has scored two or fewer goals in five straight games (0-4-1).

home.name: Arturs Silovs
home.news: In eight games this season, Silovs has already posted two shutouts, the first of his career, but he's been wildly inconsistent. The 25-year-old Latvian goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in four games but five in the other four. Silovs has a 2.87 GAA and .890 SV% in eight games (5-3-0). The Penguins enter Thursday's action as +116 home underdogs against a Utah Mammoth team that defeated them 5-4 less than two weeks ago.

away.name: Jet Greaves
away.news: Greaves has had an up-and-down start to the 2026-27 season, paving the way for more starts for Cam Talbot in recent games, but he will return to the crease on Thursday. The 25-year-old Greaves had a 31-save shutout last week in a 1-0 overtime win over the New York Rangers, which he followed up by allowing five goals on 19 shots (.737 SV%) in a 6-2 loss to the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has a pedestrian 3.34 GAA and .883 SV% in six games (2-3-0). The Blue Jackets enter Thursday's game as sizeable +220 road underdogs against a Carolina Hurricanes team that is 3-0-1 in their last four games.

home.name: Juuse Saros
home.news: Saros has had consecutive disappointing seasons, finishing with sub- .900 SV% for the first two times in his career, but is off to an encouraging start in 2026-27. Despite a modest 3-2-3 record, Saros has been serviceable with a 2.81 GAA and .906 SV% in nine games (3-2-4). He saved 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 4-3 shootout loss to the New York Islanders. The Predators enter Thursday's action as slight -100 home underdogs against a Washington Capitals team that defeated the Philadelphia Flyers 5-2 last night.

away.name: Jakub Dobes
away.news: After a breakout 2025-26 season that continued with an impressive postseason run, Dobes has struggled early in 2026-27. As a result, the Canadiens have often turned to Jacob Fowler, who has dazzled when called upon, posting an absurd 1.54 GAA and .942 SV% in seven games (6-1-0). That said, after Fowler's sensational 46-save shutout in Montreal's previous game, the team will turn to Dobes on Thursday. The 25-year-old Dobes has played only once in the past two weeks, in a 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks, where he allowed four goals on 30 shots (.867 SV%).

home.name: Jake Oettinger
home.news: Casey DeSmith saw the Stars' five-game winning streak snap in their previous game, a 5-1 loss to the New Jersey Devils. Oettinger has been tremendous to start the season and will return to the crease on Thursday. The 27-year-old American goalie has won four straight, posting a solid 1.70 GAA and .909 SV%. He has a 1.43 GAA, a .929 SV%, and three shutouts in nine games this season (6-2-1). The Stars enter Thursday's game as -165 home favourites against a Montreal Canadiens team with points in five straight games (4-0-1).
